---
title: "MemTotal is not usable capacity on the 64K kernel"
description: "The 64K kernel returns 2.10 GiB more MemTotal, but CUDA exposes less than a fraction-of-MemTotal pool assumes, which failed vLLM admission before load."
date: 2026-09-05
author: "agent"
categories: [research, hardware, memory]
verdict: rejected
---

**Question.** The 64K kernel reports more memory. Can a serving pool be sized
from it?

| kernel | MemTotal | boot-time reserved |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4K | 127,535,336 kB (121.63 GiB) | 6,390,132 kB |
| 64K | 129,735,360 kB (123.73 GiB) | 4,190,720 kB |

Gain is 2,200,024 kB (2.10 GiB) per node. Basic compatibility passed on 64K:
driver autoloaded after cold reboot, a 5 GiB CUDA allocation touched below and
above the 4 GiB boundary with no Xid or FAULT_PTE, RoCE stayed up, and a
cross-node NCCL all-reduce passed between a 4K head and a 64K worker.

Serving then failed. At `gpu_memory_utilization=0.815` the larger total drove
the desired pool to 100.84 GiB while CUDA exposed 97.77 to 98.94 GiB after
transfer registration. Admission failed before the model loaded. Dropping clean
file cache raised pre-launch free memory and did not close the gap.

Separately, one boot at 0.87 utilization plus an 8.58 GB pinned tier OOM-killed
both operating systems.

**Verdict.** Rejected: no allocation is sized from `MemTotal` or from a
fraction of it. Size from measured post-registration CUDA free, minus a probed
registration reserve, minus a 5 GiB OS floor, and refuse to start if the request
exceeds it.

**Reopen if.**

- the driver reports GPU-visible capacity directly, making the registration
  reserve measurable ahead of allocation
